page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
lines: Production of two different kinds of spores
by the same plant is called heterospory.
steps.why: The definition must carry the two facts inside the word: two kinds of spores, one plant. The book words it 'two kinds of spores from a species'; the standard form is 'by the same plant'.
common_mistakes: Writing 'two spores' instead of 'two KINDS of spores'.
Answering with homospory (one kind of spore) — the opposite term.
steps.memory_tip: Hetero = different. Heterospory = spores of two different kinds, not one.
steps.margin_note: Two lines are enough for this mark.

steps.label: The two kinds of spores

lines.text: The two kinds: microspores and megaspores

lines: Microspores are small and develop into the
and develop into the female gametophyte.
Ex: Selaginella and all seed plants.
steps.why: Naming the two spore types shows the definition is understood: the small microspore is the male line, the large megaspore is the female line.
common_mistakes: Swapping them: the MEGAspore is the larger one and forms the FEMALE gametophyte.
Leaving out the names — 'two kinds' alone does not show which two.
steps.memory_tip: Mega = large = female line. Micro = small = male line.
steps.margin_note: Name both spores; the example line is a safe extra.
